Relay topology

Mesh

The whole MeshCore mesh as a topology map — every located node from GET /api/v1/events?layer=mesh, colored by role, with the relay links from GET /api/v1/mesh/links: the server rolls up each advert's relay path over time into a durable, weighted edge list. Links fade by recency (a quiet-but-recent link is dim, not gone) and thicken with traffic; the window control trades currency for history, so an intermittent, shaky mesh reads honestly. Coverage is deliberately wide (Bay Area → Sierra). A sparse map is not an all-clear — a node is only drawn once we've heard it advertise a location.

Nodes heard

node · type · snr / rssi · hops · heard

Mesh presence is ambient INFO state: it is excluded from a place's totalActive, its severity counts, its top events and its area mode — a busy mesh does not raise an alert level, and a quiet one does not lower it. Telemetry (SNR, RSSI, hop count) is volatile and deliberately excluded from the content hash, so it never mints a revision; only a node's identity, location or status does. To ask when a node last spoke, read the event's observedAt, not telemetry.lastAdvertAt — the latter is stamped by the node's own unsynchronized clock. Missing telemetry renders as —, never as 0.
